title: Tenali Raman Tale 139 (मराठी)

full_text:
A wealthy, litigious merchant named Varadappa filed an extraordinary lawsuit before King Krishnadevaraya against a poor woodcutter named Kaliappa:
'Maharaj! Last night, I had an extraordinarily vivid and sacred dream!
In my dream, woodcutter Kaliappa broke into my stables, stole my prize riding elephant, and sold it in the market for five hundred gold coins!
Our ancient dream treatises state that dreams reveal real spiritual debts. I demand that Kaliappa pay me five hundred gold coins in restitution!'

Poor Kaliappa, who earned barely three coppers a day cutting firewood, wept in terror: 'Maharaj, I never saw an elephant in my life!'
The King was amused, but puzzled over how to dismiss the traditional dream argument without offending the religious scholars.

Tenali Raman stepped forward:
'Maharaj, Varadappa’s dream claim is completely valid according to the ancient Code of Dreams!
I shall settle the debt immediately on Kaliappa’s behalf!'

Tenali had an enormous bronze mirror placed upon a table in the center of the audience hall.
Tenali then brought out a large leather bag containing five hundred gold dinars from the royal treasury.
Tenali placed the open bag of gold directly in front of the mirror, so that five hundred gleaming gold coins were reflected with dazzling brilliance in the glass!

Tenali turned to Merchant Varadappa:
'Master Varadappa, step forward and collect your restitution!'

Varadappa reached out his hands eagerly toward the real leather bag of gold.
Tenali smacked his hand away with a fan:
'No, no, Master Varadappa! Do not touch the real gold!
Your elephant was stolen in an imaginary dream; therefore, you cannot touch real physical coins!
Look into the mirror!
Behold the five hundred gleaming gold coins reflected in the glass!
Reach out your hands, scoop up the reflected gold coins from inside the mirror, and take them home to your treasury!
A dream elephant has been paid for with mirror gold! The account is settled!'

The entire court erupted in roaring, body-shaking laughter!
Varadappa stood frozen in utter mortification, realizing how thoroughly his greed had been rebuked.
King Krishnadevaraya laughed until tears ran down his cheeks, dismissed the absurd lawsuit, and fined Varadappa twenty silver coins to be given to the poor woodcutter.
Tenali was hailed as the master of poetic justice.
moral: Claims based upon dreams have no legal standing in the waking world of justice. [MR]
